subproblems.title: Carathéodory-measurable fields have Borel a.e.-versions on σ-compact locally compact Hausdorff spaces
subproblems.statement: Let X be a Hausdorff, locally compact, σ-compact topological space with its Borel σ-algebra, μ a measure on X with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ X, N ∈ ℕ, and ν : X → ℝ^N measurable from the Carathéodory σ-algebra of the outer measure μ* induced by μ to the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^N (i.e. ν⁻¹(B) is μ*-Carathéodory measurable for every Borel B ⊆ ℝ^N). Then there is ν' : X → ℝ^N, strongly measurable for the Borel σ-algebra of X, with ν = ν' μ-almost everywhere (μ*({x : ν(x) ≠ ν'(x)}) = 0).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [LocallyCompactSpace X] [SigmaCompactSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] (μ : Measure X) (N : ℕ) (ν : X → Rn N), (∀ K : Set X, IsCompact K → μ K < ∞) → Measurable[μ.toOuterMeasure.caratheodory] ν → ∃ ν' : X → Rn N, StronglyMeasurable ν' ∧ ν =ᵐ[μ] ν'
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 6(a)-(e) of the supplied proof of gaussGreenRep_riesz_on_open. That step produces the Borel version of the field from Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 4.14 (chapter-01.txt lines 1654-1663). Here it is stated for an arbitrary Hausdorff, locally compact, σ-compact X in place of the open set U.

Notation:
- μ*(A) := inf{μ(H) : H ⊇ A Borel} is the outer measure of μ (Lean: μ.toOuterMeasure; μ A means μ*(A) for every A ⊆ X).
- A ⊆ X is μ*-Carathéodory measurable if μ*(S) = μ*(S ∩ A) + μ*(S ∖ A) for all S ⊆ X.
- 'μ-a.e.' means outside a set of outer measure 0.

1. Borel regularity of μ* (Step 6(a)). Every Borel set is μ*-Carathéodory measurable (Mathlib le_toOuterMeasure_caratheodory). Every A ⊆ X has a Borel hull H ⊇ A with μ*(H) = μ*(A) (Mathlib exists_measurable_superset / toMeasurable). So μ* is Borel regular (SimonGMT Chapter01.measure_toOuterMeasure_isBorelRegular μ).

2. A countable open cover by sets of finite measure (Step 6(b)). By σ-compactness, X = ⋃ₙ Kₙ with every Kₙ compact. As X is locally compact Hausdorff, each Kₙ has an open Vₙ ⊇ Kₙ with compact closure (Mathlib exists_isOpen_superset_and_isCompact_closure). Then μ*(Vₙ) ≤ μ(closure Vₙ) < ∞ by hypothesis, and ⋃ₙ Vₙ = X. (SimonGMT Chapter01.isOpenSigmaFinite_of_finite_compacts.)

3. Carathéodory-measurable sets are μ-null-measurable (Step 6(c)). Let A be μ*-Carathéodory measurable and fix n.
- Aₙ := A ∩ Vₙ is Carathéodory measurable: Vₙ is Borel (step 1) and the Carathéodory sets form a σ-algebra. Moreover μ*(Aₙ) ≤ μ*(Vₙ) < ∞.
- By step 1 choose a Borel Sₙ ⊇ Aₙ with μ*(Sₙ) = μ*(Aₙ). The Carathéodory identity for Aₙ with test set Sₙ reads μ*(Sₙ) = μ*(Sₙ ∩ Aₙ) + μ*(Sₙ ∖ Aₙ) = μ*(Aₙ) + μ*(Sₙ ∖ Aₙ). Since μ*(Sₙ) = μ*(Aₙ) < ∞, we get μ*(Sₙ ∖ Aₙ) = 0.
- Choose a Borel Zₙ ⊇ Sₙ ∖ Aₙ with μ*(Zₙ) = 0 and put Bₙ := Sₙ ∖ Zₙ. Then Bₙ is Borel. Bₙ ⊆ Aₙ, because a point of Sₙ outside Aₙ lies in Zₙ. And Aₙ ∖ Bₙ ⊆ Zₙ, so μ*(Aₙ ∖ Bₙ) = 0.
Now B := ⋃ₙ Bₙ is a Borel subset of A. Every x ∈ A ∖ B lies in some Vₙ, hence in Aₙ ∖ Bₙ, so μ*(A ∖ B) = 0 by countable subadditivity. (This is SimonGMT IsBorelRegularOuterMeasure.exists_borel_subset_mod_null applied with steps 1-2.) Since B ⊆ A, also μ*(B ∖ A) = 0. So A = B μ-a.e. (Mathlib ae_eq_set), and A is μ-null-measurable with Borel representative B (MeasurableSet.nullMeasurableSet together with NullMeasurableSet.congr).

4. ν is μ-null-measurable (Step 6(d)). For every Borel G ⊆ ℝ^N, ν⁻¹(G) is μ*-Carathéodory measurable by hypothesis, hence μ-null-measurable by step 3. This is precisely NullMeasurable ν μ.

5. ν is μ-a.e. measurable (Step 6(e)).
- The Borel σ-algebra of the second-countable space ℝ^N is countably generated, say by (Gₖ)ₖ.
- For each k, step 4 gives Borel sets Tₖ ⊆ ν⁻¹(Gₖ) ⊆ Wₖ with μ(Wₖ ∖ Tₖ) = 0. The set Z := ⋃ₖ (Wₖ ∖ Tₖ) is Borel and μ-null.
- Define ν̂ := ν on X ∖ Z and ν̂ := 0 on Z. Then ν̂ is Borel measurable: it is constant on the Borel set Z, and ν̂⁻¹(Gₖ) ∩ (X ∖ Z) = Tₖ ∖ Z is Borel for every generator Gₖ (on X ∖ Z the sets ν⁻¹(Gₖ) and Tₖ coincide, because Wₖ ∖ Tₖ ⊆ Z).
- ν̂ = ν outside the null set Z. (Mathlib NullMeasurable.aemeasurable.)

6. Strongly measurable version. ℝ^N is a second-countable metric space, so a Borel measurable map into it is strongly measurable. Hence ν is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (AEMeasurable.aestronglyMeasurable). Its representative ν' := AEStronglyMeasurable.mk is strongly measurable for the Borel σ-algebra of X (stronglyMeasurable_mk), and ν = ν' μ-a.e. (ae_eq_mk). This proves the claim.

Formalization note: the SimonGMT lemmas above are in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.{Basic, RadonOuterMeasure, RegularityCompletion}, all built in the pinned package. Importing Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.RadonPolarRepresentation provides all of them. In Lean, MeasurableSet[μ.toOuterMeasure.caratheodory] A is definitionally μ.toOuterMeasure.IsCaratheodory A, which is SimonGMT's IsCaratheodoryMeasurable. The Borel set B obtained from exists_borel_subset_mod_null satisfies MeasurableSet[borel X] B, which BorelSpace.measurable_eq turns into MeasurableSet B.
proof_key_steps: The outer measure μ* of the Borel measure μ is Borel regular: Borel sets are Carathéodory measurable, and every set has a Borel hull of equal outer measure.
σ-compactness, local compactness and finiteness on compacts give a countable open cover Vₙ of X with μ*(Vₙ) < ∞.
Every Carathéodory-measurable A contains a Borel B with μ*(A ∖ B) = 0, via Borel hulls and the Carathéodory identity on each A ∩ Vₙ. So A is μ-null-measurable.
Preimages of Borel sets under ν are Carathéodory measurable, hence null-measurable: ν is NullMeasurable.
The Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^N is countably generated, so ν is μ-a.e. measurable, hence μ-a.e. strongly measurable. Its strongly measurable representative ν' satisfies ν = ν' μ-a.e.

subproblems.title: Riesz representation with a Borel unit field on a σ-compact locally compact Hausdorff space
subproblems.statement: Let X be a Hausdorff, locally compact, σ-compact topological space with its Borel σ-algebra, N ∈ ℕ, and L : C_c(X; ℝ^N) → ℝ an ℝ-linear map such that for every compact K ⊆ X there is C ∈ ℝ with L(f) ≤ C for every f ∈ C_c(X; ℝ^N) with |f(x)| ≤ 1 for all x ∈ X and tsupport f ⊆ K. Then there are a Borel measure μ on X with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ X and a strongly measurable ν : X → ℝ^N with |ν(x)| = 1 for μ-a.e. x and L(f) = ∫_X ⟨f(x), ν(x)⟩ dμ(x) for every f ∈ C_c(X; ℝ^N).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [LocallyCompactSpace X] [SigmaCompactSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] (N : ℕ) (L : C_c(X, Rn N) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ), (∀ K : Set X, IsCompact K → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ f : C_c(X, Rn N), (∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ 1) → tsupport f ⊆ K → L f ≤ C) → ∃ (μ : Measure X) (ν : X → Rn N), (∀ K : Set X, IsCompact K → μ K < ∞) ∧ StronglyMeasurable ν ∧ (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ‖ν x‖ = 1) ∧ ∀ f : C_c(X, Rn N), L f = ∫ x, inner ℝ (f x) (ν x) ∂μ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 4.14 (Riesz Representation Theorem, chapter-01.txt lines 1654-1663) with H = ℝ^N, as used in Steps 5 and 6(f)-(g) of the supplied proof of gaussGreenRep_riesz_on_open. Here X is an arbitrary Hausdorff, locally compact, σ-compact space in place of U. Step 6(a)-(e) is the sibling theorem gaussGreenRep_riesz_caratheodory_borel_version (child caratheodory_borel_version).

1. The hypothesis of Theorem 4.14. For each compact K ⊆ X, the set {L(f) : f ∈ C_c(X; ℝ^N), |f(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, tsupport f ⊆ K} is bounded above by the C of the hypothesis. This is SimonGMT Chapter01.IsLocallyBoundedCcFunctional L, whose definition is: for every compact K, BddAbove (L '' {ω | (∀ x, ‖ω x‖ ≤ 1) ∧ tsupport ω ⊆ K}).

2. Riesz representation (Simon 4.14; Step 5). X is locally compact Hausdorff with its Borel σ-algebra. H := ℝ^N is a finite-dimensional, hence complete and second-countable, real inner product space. SimonGMT Chapter01.simon_theorem_4_14_caratheodory provides:
- μ₀ := vectorFunctionalEnvelopeMeasure L, a regular Borel measure on X (instance vectorFunctionalEnvelopeMeasure_regular);
- μ̄₀ := radonCaratheodoryMeasure μ₀, the outer measure μ₀* of μ₀ restricted to its Carathéodory σ-algebra;
- ν₁ : X → ℝ^N, strongly measurable for the Carathéodory σ-algebra of μ₀*, with |ν₁| = 1 μ̄₀-a.e. and L(f) = ∫_X ⟨f, ν₁⟩ dμ̄₀ for every f ∈ C_c(X; ℝ^N).
No case distinction on N is needed: the theorem covers every finite-dimensional target, including ℝ^0.

3. Finiteness on compacts. μ₀ is regular, in particular finite on compact sets: μ₀(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ X (IsCompact.measure_lt_top).

4. Borel version (Step 6(a)-(e)). A map into the metrizable Borel space ℝ^N that is strongly measurable for some σ-algebra is measurable for it (StronglyMeasurable.measurable). So ν₁ is measurable from the Carathéodory σ-algebra of μ₀* to the Borel sets of ℝ^N. With step 3, gaussGreenRep_riesz_caratheodory_borel_version applied to (X, μ₀, N, ν₁) gives a strongly measurable (Borel) ν₂ : X → ℝ^N with ν₁ = ν₂ μ₀-a.e.

5. μ̄₀ and μ₀ have the same null sets (Step 6(f)). For every A ⊆ X, μ̄₀(A) = μ₀*(A) = μ₀(A) (SimonGMT radonCaratheodoryMeasure_apply). Hence, for every property P, P holds μ̄₀-a.e. iff P holds μ₀-a.e.: both statements say that {x : ¬P(x)} has outer measure 0 (SimonGMT ae_radonCaratheodoryMeasure_iff). Consequently |ν₁| = 1 μ₀-a.e., and since ν₁ = ν₂ μ₀-a.e., also |ν₂| = 1 μ₀-a.e. Moreover ν₁ = ν₂ μ̄₀-a.e.

6. The representation (Step 6(g)). Let f ∈ C_c(X; ℝ^N).
- By step 5, ⟨f, ν₁⟩ = ⟨f, ν₂⟩ μ̄₀-a.e., so L(f) = ∫⟨f, ν₁⟩ dμ̄₀ = ∫⟨f, ν₂⟩ dμ̄₀ (integral_congr_ae).
- x ↦ ⟨f(x), ν₂(x)⟩ is strongly measurable for the Borel σ-algebra of X: f is continuous with compact support (Continuous.stronglyMeasurable_of_hasCompactSupport), ν₂ is strongly measurable, and inner products of strongly measurable maps are strongly measurable (StronglyMeasurable.inner).
- The trim of μ̄₀ to the Borel σ-algebra is μ₀, because μ̄₀(B) = μ₀(B) for Borel B. So μ̄₀- and μ₀-integrals of Borel strongly measurable integrands agree (SimonGMT integral_radonCaratheodoryMeasure, proved via integral_trim and radonCaratheodoryMeasure_trim).
Hence L(f) = ∫_X ⟨f, ν₂⟩ dμ₀.

7. Conclusion. μ := μ₀ and ν := ν₂ satisfy every claim:
- μ is a Borel measure, finite on compact sets (step 3);
- ν is strongly measurable (step 4);
- |ν| = 1 μ-a.e. (step 5);
- L(f) = ∫⟨f, ν⟩ dμ for every f ∈ C_c(X; ℝ^N) (step 6).

Formalization note: the SimonGMT declarations used above are in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.{VectorFunctionalEnvelope, RadonCaratheodoryIntegral, RadonPolarRepresentation}, built in the pinned package. Adding `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.RadonPolarRepresentation` makes all of them available.
proof_key_steps: The local bound on L is SimonGMT IsLocallyBoundedCcFunctional L, the hypothesis of Simon 4.14.

simon_theorem_4_14_caratheodory gives the regular Borel measure μ₀ = vectorFunctionalEnvelopeMeasure L and a Carathéodory-measurable ν₁. It has |ν₁| = 1 μ̄₀-a.e. and L(f) = ∫⟨f, ν₁⟩dμ̄₀ with μ̄₀ = radonCaratheodoryMeasure μ₀.
μ₀ is finite on compacts. The sibling theorem gaussGreenRep_riesz_caratheodory_borel_version gives a Borel strongly measurable ν₂ with ν₁ = ν₂ μ₀-a.e.
μ̄₀ and μ₀ agree on all sets, so they have the same a.e. statements: |ν₂| = 1 μ₀-a.e. and ν₁ = ν₂ μ̄₀-a.e.
For f ∈ C_c(X; ℝ^N), ∫⟨f, ν₁⟩dμ̄₀ = ∫⟨f, ν₂⟩dμ̄₀ = ∫⟨f, ν₂⟩dμ₀ because the last integrand is Borel strongly measurable. Take μ := μ₀, ν := ν₂.

subproblems.title: Admissible fields on an open U ⊆ ℝ^N define a locally bounded linear functional on C_c(U; ℝ^N)
subproblems.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^N open (carrying the subspace topology), and Λ : (ℝ^N → ℝ^N) → ℝ. Call g : ℝ^N → ℝ^N admissible if g is continuous with compact support and tsupport g ⊆ U. Assume Λ(g + h) = Λ(g) + Λ(h) and Λ(c g) = c Λ(g) for all admissible g, h and c ∈ ℝ. Assume also that for every compact K ⊆ U there is C ∈ ℝ with Λ(g) ≤ C for every continuous g with tsupport g ⊆ K and |g(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. Then there is an ℝ-linear map L : C_c(U; ℝ^N) → ℝ with two properties. (i) For every compact K ⊆ U (compact in the subspace U) there is C ∈ ℝ with L(f) ≤ C for every f ∈ C_c(U; ℝ^N) with |f(y)| ≤ 1 for all y ∈ U and tsupport f ⊆ K. (ii) For every admissible g there is f ∈ C_c(U; ℝ^N) with f(y) = g(y) for all y ∈ U and L(f) = Λ(g).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (U : Set (Rn N)) (Λ : (Rn N → Rn N) → ℝ), IsOpen U → (∀ g h : Rn N → Rn N, Continuous g → HasCompactSupport g → tsupport g ⊆ U → Continuous h → HasCompactSupport h → tsupport h ⊆ U → Λ (g + h) = Λ g + Λ h) → (∀ (c : ℝ) (g : Rn N → Rn N), Continuous g → HasCompactSupport g → tsupport g ⊆ U → Λ (c • g) = c * Λ g) → (∀ K : Set (Rn N), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ g : Rn N → Rn N, Continuous g → tsupport g ⊆ K → (∀ x, ‖g x‖ ≤ 1) → Λ g ≤ C) → ∃ L : C_c(U, Rn N) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ, (∀ K : Set U, IsCompact K → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ f : C_c(U, Rn N), (∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ 1) → tsupport f ⊆ K → L f ≤ C) ∧ ∀ g : Rn N → Rn N, Continuous g → HasCompactSupport g → tsupport g ⊆ U → ∃ f : C_c(U, Rn N), (∀ y : U, f y = g ↑y) ∧ L f = Λ g
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 1-4 of the supplied proof of gaussGreenRep_riesz_on_open. These steps pass from ℝ^N to the locally compact space U, as needed to apply Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 4.14 in Simon Ch. 2, (2.1)-(2.2), chapter-02.txt lines 485-496. Let ι : U → ℝ^N be the inclusion; U carries the subspace topology. A field g : ℝ^N → ℝ^N is admissible if it is continuous, has compact support and tsupport g ⊆ U.

1. Topology. U is open, so ι is an open embedding. U and ℝ^N are Hausdorff. A set A ⊆ U is compact in U iff ι(A) is compact in ℝ^N (Subtype.isCompact_iff). For S ⊆ ℝ^N, ι(ι⁻¹(S)) = U ∩ S (Subtype.image_preimage_coe).

2. Zero extension. For f ∈ C_c(U; ℝ^N) let f̃ : ℝ^N → ℝ^N be its extension by zero: f̃(ι y) = f(y) for y ∈ U, and f̃(x) = 0 for x ∉ U. In Lean f̃ = Function.extend Subtype.val f 0; the two identities are Subtype.val_injective.extend_apply and Function.extend_apply', the latter because x ∉ U is not in the range of ι.
(a) Support. T := ι(tsupport f) is compact (continuous image of a compact set), hence closed in the Hausdorff space ℝ^N, and T ⊆ U. Since f̃ vanishes outside ι(support f) ⊆ T, we get tsupport f̃ ⊆ T ⊆ U (HasCompactSupport.tsupport_extend_zero_subset). In particular f̃ has compact support (HasCompactSupport.extend_zero).
(b) Continuity (HasCompactSupport.continuous_extend_zero, which uses that U is open). A function is continuous if it is continuous at each point of its topological support. Let x ∈ tsupport f̃ ⊆ T ⊆ U, say x = ι(y). On the open set U, f̃ agrees with f ∘ ι⁻¹, and f is continuous at y. Since ι is an open embedding, f̃ is continuous at x.
Hence f̃ is admissible.
(c) Linearity of the extension. For f, f' ∈ C_c(U; ℝ^N) and c ∈ ℝ: (f + f')~ = f̃ + f̃' and (c f)~ = c f̃. Pointwise check: at x = ι(y) both sides equal f(y) + f'(y), resp. c f(y); at x ∉ U both sides are 0.
(d) If |f(y)| ≤ 1 for all y ∈ U, then |f̃(x)| ≤ 1 for all x ∈ ℝ^N. On U the value is |f(y)|; off U it is 0.
(e) If tsupport f ⊆ K ⊆ U, then tsupport f̃ ⊆ ι(tsupport f) ⊆ ι(K), by (a).

3. Definition and linearity of L (Step 4). Put L(f) := Λ(f̃).
- Additivity: for f, f' ∈ C_c(U; ℝ^N), f̃ and f̃' are admissible (step 2). The additivity hypothesis and 2(c) give L(f + f') = Λ(f̃ + f̃') = Λ(f̃) + Λ(f̃') = L(f) + L(f').
- Homogeneity: for c ∈ ℝ, the homogeneity hypothesis and 2(c) give L(c f) = Λ(c f̃) = c Λ(f̃) = c L(f).
So L is ℝ-linear.

4. The local bound (i) (Step 4). Let K ⊆ U be compact in U. Then ι(K) is compact in ℝ^N (continuous image) and ι(K) ⊆ U. The bound hypothesis gives C ∈ ℝ with Λ(g) ≤ C for every continuous g with tsupport g ⊆ ι(K) and |g| ≤ 1 everywhere. Let f ∈ C_c(U; ℝ^N) with |f| ≤ 1 on U and tsupport f ⊆ K. Then g := f̃ is continuous (2(b)), tsupport f̃ ⊆ ι(K) (2(e)) and |f̃| ≤ 1 (2(d)). Hence L(f) = Λ(f̃) ≤ C.

5. Restriction (Step 3). Let g be admissible and put f₀ := g ∘ ι : U → ℝ^N, which is continuous.
- K₀ := ι⁻¹(tsupport g) is compact in U by step 1: ι(K₀) = U ∩ tsupport g = tsupport g, which is compact because tsupport g ⊆ U.
- If y ∉ K₀ then ι(y) ∉ tsupport g, so f₀(y) = g(ι y) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport).
- So f₀ vanishes outside the compact K₀ and has compact support (HasCompactSupport.intro; U is Hausdorff).
Thus f := f₀ ∈ C_c(U; ℝ^N) and f(y) = g(ι y) for all y ∈ U.

6. f̃ = g. For x = ι(y) ∈ U: f̃(x) = f(y) = g(x). For x ∉ U: f̃(x) = 0, and x ∉ tsupport g (as tsupport g ⊆ U), so g(x) = 0. Hence f̃ = g and L(f) = Λ(f̃) = Λ(g).

7. Conclusion. L is ℝ-linear (step 3) and satisfies the local bound (i) (step 4). For every admissible g, the f of step 5 satisfies f(y) = g(y) for all y ∈ U and L(f) = Λ(g) (step 6). This is (ii).
proof_key_steps: For f ∈ C_c(U; ℝ^N) the zero extension f̃ = extend ι f 0 is continuous because U is open. It satisfies tsupport f̃ ⊆ ι(tsupport f) ⊆ U, so it is admissible; it is linear in f and preserves |·| ≤ 1.
L(f) := Λ(f̃) is ℝ-linear by the additivity and homogeneity of Λ on admissible fields.
For compact K ⊆ U, ι(K) is a compact subset of ℝ^N inside U. The bound for Λ on unit fields supported in ι(K) bounds L on unit fields supported in K.
For admissible g, the restriction g ∘ ι vanishes off the compact set ι⁻¹(tsupport g), so it lies in C_c(U; ℝ^N). Its zero extension is g, hence L(g ∘ ι) = Λ(g).

subproblems.title: Push-forward of a measure and unit field from a Borel set U ⊆ ℝ^N to ℝ^N
subproblems.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ and U ⊆ ℝ^N a Borel set, carrying the subspace topology and the subspace σ-algebra {B ∩ U : B Borel}. Let μ₀ be a measure on U with μ₀(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U. Let ν₀ : U → ℝ^N be μ₀-a.e. strongly measurable with |ν₀(y)| = 1 for μ₀-a.e. y. Then there are a Borel measure μ on ℝ^N and ν : ℝ^N → ℝ^N with: μ(ℝ^N ∖ U) = 0; μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U; ν μ-a.e. strongly measurable; |ν(x)| = 1 for μ-a.e. x; and ∫_{ℝ^N} ⟨g(x), ν(x)⟩ dμ(x) = ∫_U ⟨g(y), ν₀(y)⟩ dμ₀(y) for every function g : ℝ^N → ℝ^N (Bochner integrals, which are 0 for non-integrable integrands).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (U : Set (Rn N)) (μ₀ : Measure U) (ν₀ : U → Rn N), MeasurableSet U → (∀ K : Set U, IsCompact K → μ₀ K < ∞) → AEStronglyMeasurable ν₀ μ₀ → (∀ᵐ y ∂μ₀, ‖ν₀ y‖ = 1) → ∃ (μ : Measure (Rn N)) (ν : Rn N → Rn N), μ Uᶜ = 0 ∧ (∀ K : Set (Rn N), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K < ∞) ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable ν μ ∧ (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ‖ν x‖ = 1) ∧ ∀ g : Rn N → Rn N, ∫ x, inner ℝ (g x) (ν x) ∂μ = ∫ y, inner ℝ (g ↑y) (ν₀ y) ∂μ₀
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 7 of the supplied proof of gaussGreenRep_riesz_on_open (push-forward to ℝ^N). Let ι : U → ℝ^N be the inclusion. U carries the subspace σ-algebra {ι⁻¹(B) : B Borel} = {B ∩ U : B Borel} (in Lean, the subtype measurable space) and the subspace topology.

1. ι is a measurable embedding. ι is injective and measurable. It maps measurable sets to measurable sets: a measurable subset of U has the form B ∩ U with B Borel, and B ∩ U is Borel because U is (Mathlib MeasurableEmbedding.subtype_coe).

2. Definitions (Step 7). μ := ι_# μ₀ (Measure.map ι μ₀). ν : ℝ^N → ℝ^N is the extension of ν₀ by zero: ν(ι y) = ν₀(y) for y ∈ U and ν(x) = 0 for x ∉ U (Lean: Function.extend Subtype.val ν₀ 0 with Subtype.val_injective.extend_apply). In particular ν ∘ ι = ν₀.

3. The push-forward on arbitrary sets. For every S ⊆ ℝ^N, μ(S) = μ₀(ι⁻¹(S)) (MeasurableEmbedding.map_apply).
- '≥' holds for every measurable map.
- For '≤', let A ⊇ ι⁻¹(S) be a measurable hull in U with μ₀(A) = μ₀(ι⁻¹(S)). The set t := ι(A) ∪ (ℝ^N ∖ U) is Borel by step 1, contains S, and satisfies ι⁻¹(t) = A. Hence μ(S) ≤ μ(t) = μ₀(A) = μ₀(ι⁻¹(S)).

4. Transfer of a.e. statements. For every property P of points of ℝ^N: P holds μ-a.e. iff P(ι y) holds for μ₀-a.e. y ∈ U (MeasurableEmbedding.ae_map_iff). This is step 3 with S := {x : ¬P(x)}, since ι⁻¹(S) = {y : ¬P(ι y)}.

5. Vanishing off U. μ(ℝ^N ∖ U) = μ₀(ι⁻¹(ℝ^N ∖ U)) = μ₀(∅) = 0, by step 3.

6. Finiteness on compact subsets of U. Let K ⊆ U be compact. Then ι(ι⁻¹(K)) = U ∩ K = K is compact, so ι⁻¹(K) is compact in U (Subtype.isCompact_iff, Subtype.image_preimage_coe). By step 3 and the hypothesis, μ(K) = μ₀(ι⁻¹(K)) < ∞.

7. Transfer of a.e.-strong measurability. A map h on ℝ^N is μ-a.e. strongly measurable iff h ∘ ι is μ₀-a.e. strongly measurable (MeasurableEmbedding.aestronglyMeasurable_map_iff).
- '⇒': composition with the measurable map ι.
- '⇐': let h ∘ ι = k μ₀-a.e. with k strongly measurable on U. Extend k to a strongly measurable k̂ on ℝ^N with k̂ ∘ ι = k (MeasurableEmbedding.exists_stronglyMeasurable_extend). Then h(ι y) = k̂(ι y) for μ₀-a.e. y, so h = k̂ μ-a.e. by step 4.
Since ν ∘ ι = ν₀ is μ₀-a.e. strongly measurable, ν is μ-a.e. strongly measurable.

8. Unit length a.e. |ν(ι y)| = |ν₀(y)| = 1 for μ₀-a.e. y, so |ν| = 1 μ-a.e. by step 4.

9. Change of variables. Let g : ℝ^N → ℝ^N be arbitrary and F(x) := ⟨g(x), ν(x)⟩. Then ∫_{ℝ^N} F dμ = ∫_U F(ι y) dμ₀(y) (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map).
- If F is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, this is the change-of-variables formula for push-forwards (integral_map).
- Otherwise, by step 7, F ∘ ι is not μ₀-a.e. strongly measurable either, and both Bochner integrals are 0 by definition.
Since F(ι y) = ⟨g(ι y), ν₀(y)⟩, this gives ∫⟨g, ν⟩ dμ = ∫_U ⟨g(y), ν₀(y)⟩ dμ₀(y).

10. Conclusion. μ and ν satisfy all claims: μ(ℝ^N ∖ U) = 0 (step 5); μ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U (step 6); ν is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (step 7); |ν| = 1 μ-a.e. (step 8); the integral identity holds for every g (step 9).
proof_key_steps: U Borel makes the inclusion ι : U → ℝ^N a measurable embedding.
Set μ := ι_#μ₀ and ν := the zero extension of ν₀, so ν ∘ ι = ν₀.
For a measurable embedding, μ(S) = μ₀(ι⁻¹S) for every S. Hence μ(ℝ^N ∖ U) = 0, μ(K) = μ₀(ι⁻¹K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U, and a.e. statements transfer along ι.
a.e.-strong measurability transfers along ι, so ν is μ-a.e. strongly measurable and |ν| = 1 μ-a.e.
Change of variables ∫F dμ = ∫F∘ι dμ₀ holds for every F, which gives ∫⟨g, ν⟩dμ = ∫⟨g∘ι, ν₀⟩dμ₀.
